title: Halo Crew Capsule
description: A single-seat capsule. It's cramped, and it's the only thing between you and the outside.

title: Halo Heat Shield
description: Goes under the Halo, faces the fire, and chars away so the capsule doesn't. Once.

title: Canopy Recovery Pack
description: A canopy that mounts on the nose. Deploy it below 300 m/s or watch it shred.

title: Parting Ring
description: Separates what's above it from what's below it, once, and loudly.

title: Punt Hull
description: A long, flat, sealed box. It floats because it's mostly air, and it goes straight because it's much longer than it is wide, so the water pushes back hard on its sides and hardly at all on its bow. Build it lying down.

title: Cask-2 Propellant Tank
description: Two metres of propellant in a thin aluminium shell.

title: Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: Four metres of the same idea.

title: Ember Lifter Engine
description: A gimballed lifter engine. It's not efficient, but it'll get you off the pad.

title: Vesper Vacuum Engine
description: Built for vacuum. It's nearly useless in the atmosphere, and excellent once you're out of it.

title: Zephyr Air-Breather
description: It breathes the air it flies through, so it only carries fuel, and sips that. Its thrust falls away with the air, to nothing at all in vacuum. It's an engine for staying in the sky, not for leaving it.

title: Vane Stabiliser
description: Keeps the pointy end forward while there's still air to push against. It's a stabiliser, not a control surface, so it doesn't deflect.

title: Plank Wing
description: A wing is a fin with enough area to hold something up. It's the same module and the same code, and only the numbers are different. Area is most of the difference.

title: Elevon
description: A control surface. It deflects with the stick, and which axis it drives depends on where you bolt it, not on what it's called. Its authority is kept modest on purpose, because at flying speed a surface this size can make more force than the wings it's trimming.

title: Spire Nose Cone
description: It costs mass, and saves more drag than it costs.

title: Stilt Landing Leg
description: A sprung leg with 0.4 m of travel. Deploy it before you need it, because a stowed leg touches nothing.

title: Tread Roller
description: A sprung driven wheel. It rolls freely forwards and backwards and grips across, and that split is what makes a rover a rover instead of a sledge.

title: Gear Wheel
description: An undercarriage wheel with no drive. It rolls, steers on the ground, and otherwise stays out of the way. It's what an aircraft stands on, not what moves it.

title: Nudge Thruster Block
description: Four thrusters and a little monopropellant. They're sized so a set of them can break a landed module free of friction and walk it into place, which a main engine can't do.

title: Sparrow Cockpit
description: One seat under a bubble canopy, with the nose ahead of it. It's where you fly an aircraft from.

title: Kestrel Cockpit
description: Two seats in tandem under a long canopy. It's heavier than the Sparrow, with room for a passenger.

title: Short Fuselage
description: An airframe section with fuel in it. It's round and smooth, and it's the thing everything else on an aircraft bolts to, with mounts along its length so wings and gear can go where the balance needs them.

title: Long Fuselage
description: An airframe section with fuel in it. It's round and smooth, and it's the thing everything else on an aircraft bolts to, with mounts along its length so wings and gear can go where the balance needs them.

title: Tailcone
description: Tapers an airframe to a point at the back, where a blunt end would drag a wake behind it.

title: Swift Wing
description: A small straight wing with an aileron on its outer half. For light aircraft, and tailplanes on big ones.

title: Swept Wing
description: The leading edge is swept back and the trailing edge is straight. It's faster and less forgiving than a straight wing.

title: Delta Wing
description: A great triangle with elevons along its trailing edge. It pitches and rolls on its own, and it wants speed.

title: Rudder Tail
description: A vertical tail with a rudder. Bolted on top of the fuselage it yaws. The geometry decides, as always.

title: Merlin Propeller
description: A piston engine turning a three-bladed propeller. It has modest thrust, it's very frugal, and it pulls from the front.

title: Main Gear
description: The main undercarriage: an oleo strut and a wide wheel, with brakes. It goes just behind the centre of mass.

title: Nose Gear
description: A nose wheel that steers, on its own strut. It carries a little of the weight and all of the steering.

title: Tail Wheel
description: A small castoring wheel for a taildragger's tail. It keeps the tail off the runway, and steers.

title: Buggy Chassis
description: A four-wheel frame with a deck. The wheels go on its corners, underneath, with a cab or cargo on top.

title: Hauler Chassis
description: A long six-wheel frame. It's heavy and stable, and it's the base for anything that has to carry something.

title: Rover Cab
description: Two seats behind a raked windscreen, out of the weather. It drives the rover it sits on.

title: Open Seat
description: A seat, a wheel and a roll bar. It's light, and the view is excellent.

title: Scout Wheel
description: A small driven wheel for light rovers. It's quick to spin up, and small stones feel big.

title: Crawler Wheel
description: A big lugged off-road wheel with long travel. It climbs what the others won't, and carries weight while it does.

title: Cargo Rack
description: A railed platform for carrying things. It mounts on a deck.

title: Light Bar
description: A row of lamps. They're mostly for looking at, but they do make a rover look like it means it.

title: Rung Ladder
description: Two point four metres of rungs, to climb from the ground to the hatch. Someone on EVA takes hold with GRAB.

title: Glint Sun Panel
description: A fixed sheet of cells for the side of anything. It makes what it can from the sun it faces, and nothing in shadow.

title: Kite Sun Wing
description: A folding wing of cells that turns itself to the sun. It folds out when staged or told to, and out in thick air it tears off.

title: Hoard Battery Pack
description: Two hundred units of charge in a box. For the night side, and the long way round.

title: Spark Fuel Cell
description: Turns monopropellant into charge. It comes on by itself when the batteries run low, and goes off again when they're well up. It needs monopropellant on the same stage.

title: Reed Whip Antenna
description: A long whip aerial. It reaches far enough to hear Terra from Luna, with nothing in the way. It doesn't relay anything.

title: Beacon Relay Dish
description: A folding dish that reaches right across Terra's pull, and passes on what other craft send it. Put a few round Terra, or one past Luna.

title: Great Dish
description: A wide folding dish that hears across the whole system, out to Ultima, if home is listening. It relays what other craft send it.

title: Glow Isotope Generator
description: A slow nuclear warmth turned into charge, day and night, near the sun or far beyond it. It's heavy, and never quick, but out among the giants, where panels only see a sliver of the sun, it's what keeps a probe alive.

title: Auger Drill
description: Digs ore and water out of the ground under it, when it's on the ground, still, and powered. Its bit swings down when you switch it on, and how much comes up depends on the ground.

title: Small Converter
description: Refines ore and water into propellant, and water into a little monopropellant too, from the tanks on its own stage. It's slow, heavy and hungry for charge, but a lander carrying one never needs a base.

title: Survey Scanner
description: Maps what the ground holds. From a low orbit over the poles it surveys a whole world in half an orbit, for everyone's map, and near the ground it reads what's below.

title: Bow Section
description: The front of a hull, raked up to a stem. It parts the water, and joins a mid section or a stern behind it.

title: Mid Section
description: A plain length of hull. Add as many as the boat needs to be long.

title: Stern Section
description: The back of a hull: a flat transom for a motor, and room above for a wheelhouse.

title: Skiff Hull
description: A small V-hulled boat. It cuts through a chop the punt would slap across, and it tips over more easily too.

title: Cutter Hull
description: A long, deep hull with a keel, for open water. It carries a lot, holds a course, and turns like a ship.

title: Wheelhouse
description: A cabin with windows all round, so you can steer a boat from somewhere dry.

title: Mote Probe Core
description: Flies a craft with nobody in it, with reaction wheels, a small battery and a short aerial. It only works while it can hear home, either a ground station or a relay that can.

title: Outboard Motor
description: A motor hung off the transom, with its propeller in the water below. It swings to steer, and only pushes while the propeller is wet.

title: Rudder
description: A blade under the stern that turns with the steering. Water is dense, so a small rudder steers a big boat.

title: Keel
description: A deep fin under the hull. It stops the boat sliding sideways in a turn or a crosswind, and its weight keeps it upright.

title: Skeg
description: A small keel for a small boat: a weighted fin under the hull that keeps it from skidding sideways in a turn, and from being rolled over by its own motor.

title: Stabilator
description: An all-moving tailplane, where the whole surface turns, not a strip at its back. It has enough authority to lift a heavy nose off the runway.

title: Docking Ring
description: A docking ring for craft of the standard width. Bring two together slowly and roughly lined up and they draw each other in and latch. They can let go again.

title: Docking Ring, Small
description: A small docking ring for probes and light craft. It only mates with another small ring.

title: Tow Hitch (Ball)
description: A tow ball for the back of a rover. Back up to a trailer's coupling and it couples, and whatever is towed swings behind on it.

title: Tow Hitch (Coupling)
description: A drawbar and coupling for the front of a trailer. It couples onto a rover's tow ball.

title: Winch
description: A drum of line with a hook on the end, for the front or back of a rover. Hook it onto another craft, or onto the ground, a tree or a rock, and wind in. It's how you get yourself out of a ditch, or drag someone else out of one.

title: Mooring Clamp
description: A clamp for the side of a hull. Bring two boats alongside, clamp to clamp, and they raft up into one.

title: Sloop Rig
description: A mast with a mainsail, for a skiff or a punt. It trims itself to the wind, and the throttle sets how much sail is out, from furled to full. It can't sail closer than about forty degrees to the wind, so beat up to it in zigzags.

title: Cutter Rig
description: A tall mast and a big mainsail for a cutter's hull. It trims itself to the wind, and the throttle reefs it, from furled to full. In a blow, take some sail in or she'll lie right over.

title: Broad Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: A Cask twice as wide, with four times the propellant for every metre of it.

title: Broad Cask-8 Propellant Tank
description: Eight metres of the broad kind. It's what a first stage is mostly made of.

title: Ore Bin
description: Holds 150 units of ore, a tonne and a half of rock, for a converter, a refinery, or the haul home. It launches empty.

title: Broad Ore Bin
description: A tanker's hold: 800 units of ore, eight tonnes of it, 2.5 m across. It launches empty.

title: Water Tank
description: Holds 200 units of water melted out of ice, which is the easiest thing there is to make propellant from. It launches empty.

title: Forge Lifter Engine
description: The broad lifter. It's enough to put a moonshot on its way, and it shakes the ground doing it.

title: Broad Parting Ring
description: A Parting Ring for the broad stacks. It drops a spent first stage, and pushes harder doing it.

title: Taper
description: From the broad stacks down to the narrow, so you can put a Cask-width stage on a broad one.

title: Shroud Half
description: Half of a Shroud's shell, thrown off when it opens.

title: Shroud
description: A fairing. Put whatever rides on top on its ring, and it stands a smooth shell around it, out of the air, cool and slippery, until it's staged, when the shell falls open in two.

title: Hotshell
description: A Shroud built for Caligo. Its shell stands a hundred and fifty times Terra's air pressure and the heat underneath it, and keeps whatever rides inside alive down there, for as long as it stays shut.

title: Crew Member
description: Someone out of their craft, in a suit with a jetpack on the back.

title: Flag
description: Planted: someone was here.

title: Pearl Pressure Sphere
description: One seat inside a steel ball, with a window in its nose. It's good down to three hundred metres or so. Below that the sea starts to win.

title: Abyss Sphere
description: Titanium a hand's width thick around one seat. It's heavier than the water it pushes aside, and good for the bottom of the deepest trench.

title: Nautilus Hull
description: A pressure hull with room for two and a bank of cells in its keel. It's rated to a kilometre and a half.

title: Trim Tank
description: Let the sea in and it goes down, and blow it out and it comes up. It's rated as deep as the Pearl.

title: Deep Trim Tank
description: The Trim Tank with thicker walls, for the Nautilus's depths.

title: Abyssal Trim Tank
description: Walls that can stand the weight of seven kilometres of sea.

title: Deep Cell
description: Charge in a case built for the deep. The Hoard's case gives way below two hundred metres.

title: Abyssal Cell
description: The Deep Cell, cased for the bottom of the trench.

title: Syntactic Float
description: Glass beads in resin, solid all the way through, and lighter than water however deep it goes. It's what keeps a heavy sphere off the bottom.

title: Screw Drive
description: An electric motor in a sealed pod, turning a five-bladed screw in a duct. It runs on the batteries, because there's no air down there to burn anything in.

title: Water Jet
description: A pump that draws the water in through a grate under the stern and throws it out astern. There's nothing hanging in the water to drag, so a boat with one is several times quicker than with an outboard, and the nozzle swings to steer. Only pushes while the intake is in the water.

title: Jet Pump
description: A small water jet for a jet ski or a tender. The nozzle swings to steer, and it only pushes while the intake is in the water.

title: Jet Ski Hull
description: A short, wide planing hull for one, made to be thrown about at speed. Put a saddle on top and a jet pump on the back.

title: Runabout Hull
description: A decked planing hull, a little bigger than the skiff's, with a cockpit that drains itself over the side. Made for a water jet on the transom and a sea that comes aboard.

title: Saddle
description: A seat you sit astride, with handlebars in front of it, for a jet ski or anything small. Nothing between you and the spray, and you lean into the turns.

title: Dive Planes
description: A small wing that tilts with the stick. On a submarine's side, it pitches her nose down to dive, or up to climb.

title: Lead Keel
description: A weight of lead slung under a submarine's hull. Down there nothing holds a craft upright except weight kept low, and this keeps her level as she dives.

title: Deep Lamp
description: A floodlight sealed for the deep, lighting the water and the floor around it. Below a few hundred metres it's the only light there is.

title: Sonar Array
description: Pings the sea and listens. It tells you the depth under the keel, and which way the nearest of the sea's named places lies, out to two kilometres.

title: Rotor Head
description: A helicopter's main rotor on its mast: four long blades on an engine that burns propellant. The throttle is the collective, and the stick tilts its lift to fly it about. It twists the craft the other way as it turns, so it wants a tail rotor to hold the heading.

title: Tail Rotor
description: A small rotor that pushes sideways at the end of a tail boom. It holds the heading against the main rotor's twist, and the stick turns the craft with it.

title: Drone Rotor
description: A small electric rotor in a guard ring, for drones. Four or more of them on a frame, and the craft steers by speeding some up and slowing others.

title: Lift Fan
description: An electric fan in a duct that blows straight down, to hold up and steer a platform. Hang them under the corners.

title: Bubble Cockpit
description: A helicopter's cabin for two, with a clear bubble for a nose. The rotor goes on its roof, a boom on its tail, and skids underneath.

title: Tail Boom
description: A slim boom to carry a tail rotor well back from the main one.

title: Landing Skids
description: A pair of skids to stand a helicopter on.

title: Drone Frame
description: A light cross of arms for a drone, with a rotor at the end of each and room in the middle for a core and a battery.

title: Keeper Core
description: A flight computer that holds a craft still where you leave it: in the air on rotors, fans, gas or engines pointing down, or on the water. Switch it on with HOLD STATION. It flies a craft with nobody in it while it can hear home.

title: Balloon Envelope
description: A round envelope of light gas, with a skirt of ropes to hang a basket from. It lifts about three hundred kilograms near the ground on Terra, and less the higher it goes, until it floats. RISE and SINK work its ballonet.

title: Balloon Basket
description: A wicker basket for two, with a small battery for the ballonet's pump. Hang it under a balloon.

title: Gas Cell
description: A big box of light gas, eight metres on a side and fourteen tall, for floating a platform or a heavy airship. It lifts nearly a tonne near the ground on Terra.

title: Airship Envelope
description: A long streamlined envelope of light gas for an airship, thirty-six metres from nose to tail. Hang a gondola under the middle and a power car with a propeller behind it, and put fins on its tail.

title: Pontoon
description: A sealed float seven metres long, to hold up a platform on the sea. Put four under a sea deck.

title: Side Recovery Pack
description: A canopy for the side of a stack, for whatever has a port or a cone on top. Two or three round a stage bring it down whole.

title: Heavy Recovery Pack
description: The big one, for the side of a broad stack. It's more than twice a nose canopy's drag, so a spent first stage can come down to be flown again.

title: Side Clamp
description: Holds a booster on the side of a stack, and lets it go outward, once. Put the clamp on the core, then the booster on the clamp.

title: Feed Clamp
description: A Side Clamp with a fuel line through it. The booster it holds feeds the core's engines too, and is drunk first, so it's empty when you let it go.

title: Lantern Vacuum Engine
description: A vacuum engine for the broad stacks. It lifts a broad upper stage the way a Vesper lifts a narrow one, and it's just as poor in air.

title: Broad Nose Cone
description: A Spire for the broad stacks. It closes off the top of a broad booster or a stage with nothing on it.

title: Trio Crew Capsule
description: A broad capsule for three, with room to move and a window each. It sits on a broad stack, and wants a Broad Heat Shield under it to come home.

title: Broad Heat Shield
description: Goes under the Trio, faces the fire, and chars away so the capsule doesn't. Once.

title: Grand Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: Three Casks across. A base module stands on it the same as on its foundation, so it can lift one.

title: Grand Cask-8 Propellant Tank
description: Eight metres of the grand kind, for a first stage that lifts whole bases.

title: Anvil Lifter Engine
description: The grand lifter. It's what you put under a base module or a crewed moon lander, and the pad shakes a long way off.

title: Grand Parting Ring
description: A Parting Ring for the grand stacks, with the push to match.

title: Grand Taper
description: From the grand stacks down to the broad, so a broad stage can sit on a grand one.

title: Grand Nose Cone
description: A nose cone for the grand stacks.

title: Girder
description: Two metres of lattice. Stack them end to end, or hang them off anything's side, to build a tower, a gantry or a frame.

title: Long Girder
description: Six metres of lattice, for the tall parts of a tower or the long span of a bridge.

title: Beam
description: Four metres of solid steel beam. It's heavier than a girder and stiffer, for the bits that take the load.

title: Deck Plate
description: A three-metre square of deck, to walk on, land on, or build on. Join them edge to edge for a bigger floor.

title: Junction
description: A half-metre block with a join on every face, where girders and beams meet and turn corners.

title: Brace
description: A light steel strut for the side of anything: a leg for a deck, a prop under a gantry arm, or a stiffener between two stacks.

title: Wide Bow
description: The front of a ship's hull, four and a half metres across, raked up to a tall stem so it rides over a sea instead of into it. A wide mid section or stern joins behind it.

title: Wide Mid Section
description: Five metres of ship's hull, four and a half across. Add as many as the ship needs to be long, and there's room on deck for cargo or a crane.

title: Wide Stern
description: The back of a ship's hull, with a fuel tank in the bottom of it and a transom for an inboard engine. The wheelhouse usually goes up here.

title: Marine Diesel
description: A diesel down in the hull turning a big four-bladed propeller on a shaft out under the stern. It doesn't swing, so a ship with one steers on its rudder. It burns what's in the stern's tank as well as its own, and charges the batteries while it runs.

title: Electric Drive
description: A motor in a pod under the stern, running on the batteries. It's quiet and carries no fuel, and it goes as far as the charge does. Like a diesel, it steers on a rudder.

title: Ship's Rudder
description: A rudder four times the size of a boat's, hung under a ship's stern behind the propeller. It's what turns a ship with an inboard engine.

title: Ship's Battery Bank
description: Four thousand units of charge in a steel box for a ship's hold or deck. Enough to run an electric drive flat out for an hour.

title: Schooner Rig
description: A fourteen metre mast with a gaff mainsail, for a ship's deck. It trims itself to the wind and the throttle reefs it. Two of them, fore and aft, make a schooner.

title: Square Rig
description: A twenty metre mast crossed by three yards, with a square sail on each. It's the most sail there is, and it's happiest with the wind behind it. The throttle reefs it, from furled to full.

title: Ship's Keel
description: A deep fin keel for a ship, with four tonnes of lead in a bulb along its foot. It grips the water hard enough to sail close to the wind without sliding off to leeward, and its weight keeps her on her feet when the wind heels her.

title: Barge Bow
description: The front of a barge: its bottom raked up to the deck so it pushes the water under it instead of ahead of it. A barge section or a barge stern joins behind it.

title: Barge Section
description: Ten metres of flat-decked barge, ten across and three deep. Join as many as you need. The deck's flat and strong enough to drive, park, or land on.

title: Barge Stern
description: The back of a barge, square, with a transom for a motor if it's to go under its own power, and a flat end for a tug to push against.

title: Towing Winch
description: A ship's towing winch: sixty metres of heavy line on a drum, led out over the stern to whatever it's asked to take in tow, a barge, a ship or a platform. It hooks onto a tow bitt if there's one in reach, and pulls with two hundred kilonewtons before the drum slips.

title: Tow Bitt
description: A pair of iron posts to make a towline fast to. A winch hooks onto one of these before anything else on a craft, so the tow takes hold where it's meant to.

title: Push Knees
description: Two upright timbers faced with rubber, on the stem of a tug, for pushing a barge or a ship along instead of towing it. They take the knocks the bow would otherwise.

title: Flight Deck
description: Twenty metres square of floating steel, three deep, with a flat deck on top to land on. Join them on any side to make a platform as big as you like: two for a helicopter or a rocket to come down on, a row of eight for a plane. Engines hang off its back edge, a rudder under it.

title: Tailhook
description: An arm under a plane's tail with a hook on the end. It swings down with the landing gear, and on a deck it catches an arresting wire, which stops the plane in sixty metres.

title: Arresting Gear
description: Three steel wires across a deck, four metres apart, for a plane with a tailhook to catch. The wire pays out under the deck and stops the plane in sixty metres, no harder than four g.

title: Catapult
description: A seventy metre track in a deck with a shuttle in it. Taxi a plane onto the near end, open the throttle all the way with the brakes off, and it throws the plane off the far end at sixty metres a second.
